title: History, snapshots, usage and preferences on the API, over the dev object store
goal: What a session leaves behind and what a workspace uses are served by the running API: the session history and snapshots over an S3-compatible store (the relay's durable log writes to it too), usage reports and the usage summary, and notification preferences; the local stack has the store, so a client that was away longer than the relay's memory gets the rest.
scope_in: `apps/api/src/data.ts` builds the history store, history service, snapshot service (its own audit emitter over `SNAPSHOT_AUDIT_ACTIONS`), usage ingest, usage summary and notification preference services from the API context; their routes join `modules.ts` (GET and DELETE `/v1/sessions/{id}/history`, the snapshot begin, commit and latest routes, `POST /v1/usage/events`, `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/usage/summary`, `GET` and `PUT /v1/notification-preferences`).
`OBJECT_STORE_*` in the API's configuration (all four keys or none; a half-set store is a configuration error); history and snapshots are skipped with one log line each when it is absent.
The entitlement check reads the monthly quota counters (`queue_items_month`, `hosted_minutes_month`) through the usage module instead of allowing every metered action.

`pnpm dev:api` and `pnpm dev:relay` point at the dev stack's MinIO (the `history` bucket) so the relay's durable log and replay work locally; `pnpm dev:full-check` exercises history, snapshots, usage and preferences against the live stack.
scope_out: The worker that fills the counters (B109) and the purge of stored history (B055's hook, run by B109).
Billing, webhook, admin and release routes, which need credentials or a payment provider.
build_against: The B012 dev stack (Postgres, Redis, MinIO) for `pnpm dev:full-check`, and the in-memory stores of the module tests.
interfaces: HTTP: the history, snapshot, usage and preference routes of CT-API-SESSIONS, CT-API-USAGE and CT-API-NOTIFY.
acceptance: With an object store configured, a session's frames written by the relay are returned by `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/history?after_seq=0`, and a snapshot uploaded through the client can be downloaded again (checked live by `pnpm dev:full-check`).
Without an object store the API starts, leaves out history and snapshots with one `api.module_skipped` line each, and still serves usage and preferences (test).
A device's usage report is stored and the usage summary reads; the entitlement check refuses a metered action once its monthly counter reaches the plan's limit (test with in-memory counters).
A half-set `OBJECT_STORE_*` configuration refuses to start and names the bad keys, never their values (test).

The relay writes every sequenced frame to the object store's history bucket locally, so a client that reconnects after a gap longer than the relay keeps gets the missing frames through the history route (checked live).
`DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/history` by the host removes the history and snapshots of the session and writes a `history.purge` audit event (test).
tests: app.build.test.ts: the modules with and without an object store.
Config tests for the object store keys.
data.test.ts: the services built with and without an object store.
guardrails: MUST NOT put object-store credentials, tokens or history content in logs.
MUST keep history and snapshot routes users-only: API keys are refused.
MUST NOT widen the history and snapshot access rules: a guest reads history only when the session shares it (B055's `mayRead`).
failure_modes: Object store unreachable -> the history routes answer 503 with `retry_after_s`; the rest of the API is unaffected.
Counters unreadable -> the entitlement check allows the action and counts `entitlements.quota_check_failed`, as B080 specifies.
notes: Stacked after B106. Also changes (does not own) apps/api/src/{config,context,modules}.ts, tools/dev/{api,relay}.ts and docs/api-service.md (B102, B103). The counters stay at zero locally until B109's worker runs.
